newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Sax index slightly up led by Slovnaft.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Sax index slightly up led by Slovnaft.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with gains to oil refiner Slovnaft pushing the SAX index up 2.25 points to 192.09

Brokers said low liquidity was still the dominant characteristic of trading on the bourse, pointing to the fact that a single block deal with Slovnaft, albeit a large one, could set the direction for the whole market.
Slovnaft gained 40 crowns to close at 850, trading 52,896 shares.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed down 10 crowns at 1,820, with 96 stocks changing hands.
"Nafta is definitely not a sexy issue at the moment, but a I think its current situation on the market does not reflect the true value of the share," said Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt.
But brokers said low volumes in Nafta made it hard for them to predict future developments with the issue.
Dealers said they expected flat trading on the bourse over the next few days, with the possibility of further slight declines.
"There are certain indications of an increase in interest among larger investors, but it seems that the offer prices have not yet fallen to the demanded levels," Krutil said.
Overall volume rose to 386,740 shares from 215,626 on Friday. Turnover increased to 260.95 million crowns, from 156.98 million.
